# gh-1570 rework — the two incident-driven blocking threads fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two open review threads remained after the APPROVE re-review of `24dad1d4` — both
filed from the **real incident of 2026-10-12** (a machine updating fa
`1.0.556 → 1.0.564` was bricked at boot). Both are BLOCKING and both are fixed
here with RED→GREEN tests:

1. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability.** The
   record-scoped slot derivation (`FA_KEY_<HOST>_<RECORD>`) changed meaning
   across versions and nothing recovered slots stored by older builds: the key
   existed in the secure store under the pre-update slot name
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) while the pinned slot
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) resolved empty — "missing API key". A slot
   name is a cross-version contract; a derivation change must recover old slots.
2. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCPc` — a missing key must never hard-exit the
   binary.** The aggregate outcome of an all-key-missing role chain
   (`entries.isEmpty` → plain `ConfigException` → `_fail`) process-exited the
   CLI on a RECOVERABLE condition — the user was locked out of the very tool
   the error message told them to repair with (`/key set`). gh-760 already
   established "degrade, never brick" for version skew; a missing key gets the
   same treatment.

All other threads on this PR are either resolved (fixed + replied in the
previous legs, re-reviewed APPROVE on `24dad1d4`) or machine notices; each open
thread received a reply — see `outputs/review_replies.json`.

## Approach

**Thread 1 (key-slot stability) — recovery + migration, derivation untouched**
(re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class being
fixed):

- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})`
  (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) — the cross-version slot family of ONE
  endpoint, canonical first: the record-scoped slot plus the host-scoped shape
  the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the incident's pair).
- `ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`)
  — an explicit pin stays first choice; an EMPTY pin now falls back to the
  endpoint's slot family before the ref is declared key-missing (the gh-1000
  AC2 hint semantics unchanged: a still-missing pin names the pin).
- `roleKeyNames` (`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`) — the secrets snapshot preloads
  the whole family (pin fallback set included), so store-backed values are
  visible to the fallback.
- **Boot-time migration** (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`,
  `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`, wired in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`
  right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution): for every
  known (endpoint, record) pair — saved custom registry entries plus the roles
  chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is
  COPIED onto the canonical slot. Non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, a
  rollback keeps working); the OS keychain is explicitly in scope
  (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through); each move prints a stderr notice
  naming both slots; an unavailable/failing keychain degrades to a notice
  (resolution still falls back), never a boot failure.

**Thread 2 (missing key never bricks) — typed degradable contract:**

- New `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException`
  (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) — the degradable
  "no usable chain entry" shape; `UnknownProviderRoleException` re-parented
  under it (public API compatible; version skew stays distinguishable, the
  boot treats both identically). `chainFor`'s aggregate outcome throws the
  degradable base for the key-missing shape too — the old plain
  `ConfigException` stance is what bricked the incident machine.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` catches `on UnusableRoleChainException` → loud stderr
  warning with the resolver's named skip reasons → falls back to the
  configured single provider/model (the whole-resolver drop stays BY DESIGN
  per the gh-760 review). Plain `ConfigException` still maps to `_fail` for
  genuinely broken configs.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` — `UnusableRoleChainException`
  degrade base; empty-pin slot-family fallback; docs.
- `lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` (the cross-version
  slot family).
- `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart` — `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (+ the
  `KeySlotMigrationSource` record).
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `roleKeyNames` preloads the slot family.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot wiring: migration pass after preload; the roles
  block degrades on `UnusableRoleChainException`.
- `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — the incident REG test (key
  under the previous release's slot resolves); the missing-key aggregate
  re-pinned to the DEGRADE subtype (typed classification guards kept).
- `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` — 4 migration tests (copy+notice,
  canonical-populated no-op, unavailable store quiet, failing-write fallback).
- `test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` shape pins.
- `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart` — the boot-level IT
  (real binary): all-key-missing roles ⇒ exit 0, skipped entries NAMED, turn
  completes on the fallback.

## Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN, each verified against the unfixed code:
  - the incident REG test fails without the empty-pin fallback;
  - the missing-key degrade test fails while `chainFor` still throws plain
    `ConfigException`;
  - the boot IT fails (exit 254 — the exact incident brick) while the boot
    still caught only `UnknownProviderRoleException`.
- Targeted suites: `dart test test/model_roles/ test/cli/startup_test.dart
  test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart
  test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — **497 passed**.
- Boot IT (integration tag): the gh-760 poisoned-provider family incl. the new
  degrade case — green.
- `dart analyze` — 0 issues on all touched files; `dart format` clean on all
  touched files (the pre-existing whole-tree test drift is untouched, diff
  stays scoped).
- `crap4dart check --baseline` — gates pass (threshold untouched); the loc
  gate (`crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc`) passes.
- Full suite `dart test` — running against the frozen tree; result recorded in
  the run log (job `sh-71-hn60g1u9a3ygx50u`).

The Flutter app shares `ModelRolesResolver` (best-effort guarded, no
process-exit surface), so both fixes apply there unchanged.

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — the two incident-driven blocking threads fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two open review threads remained after the APPROVE re-review of `24dad1d4` — both
filed from the **real incident of 2026-10-12** (a machine updating fa
`1.0.556 → 1.0.564` was bricked at boot). Both are BLOCKING and both are fixed
here with RED→GREEN tests:

1. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability.** The
   record-scoped slot derivation (`FA_KEY_<HOST>_<RECORD>`) changed meaning
   across versions and nothing recovered slots stored by older builds: the key
   existed in the secure store under the pre-update slot name
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) while the pinned slot
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) resolved empty — "missing API key". A slot
   name is a cross-version contract; a derivation change must recover old slots.
2. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCPc` — a missing key must never hard-exit the
   binary.** The aggregate outcome of an all-key-missing role chain
   (`entries.isEmpty` → plain `ConfigException` → `_fail`) process-exited the
   CLI on a RECOVERABLE condition — the user was locked out of the very tool
   the error message told them to repair with (`/key set`). gh-760 already
   established "degrade, never brick" for version skew; a missing key gets the
   same treatment.

All other threads on this PR are either resolved (fixed + replied in the
previous legs, re-reviewed APPROVE on `24dad1d4`) or machine notices; each open
thread received a reply — see `outputs/review_replies.json`.

## Approach

**Thread 1 (key-slot stability) — recovery + migration, derivation untouched**
(re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class being
fixed):

- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})`
  (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) — the cross-version slot family of ONE
  endpoint, canonical first: the record-scoped slot plus the host-scoped shape
  the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the incident's pair).
- `ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`)
  — an explicit pin stays first choice; an EMPTY pin now falls back to the
  endpoint's slot family before the ref is declared key-missing (the gh-1000
  AC2 hint semantics unchanged: a still-missing pin names the pin).
- `roleKeyNames` (`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`) — the secrets snapshot preloads
  the whole family (pin fallback set included), so store-backed values are
  visible to the fallback.
- **Boot-time migration** (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`,
  `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`, wired in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`
  right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution): for every
  known (endpoint, record) pair — saved custom registry entries plus the roles
  chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is
  COPIED onto the canonical slot. Non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, a
  rollback keeps working); the OS keychain is explicitly in scope
  (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through); each move prints a stderr notice
  naming both slots; an unavailable/failing keychain degrades to a notice
  (resolution still falls back), never a boot failure.

**Thread 2 (missing key never bricks) — typed degradable contract:**

- New `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException`
  (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) — the degradable
  "no usable chain entry" shape; `UnknownProviderRoleException` re-parented
  under it (public API compatible; version skew stays distinguishable, the
  boot treats both identically). `chainFor`'s aggregate outcome throws the
  degradable base for the key-missing shape too — the old plain
  `ConfigException` stance is what bricked the incident machine.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` catches `on UnusableRoleChainException` → loud stderr
  warning with the resolver's named skip reasons → falls back to the
  configured single provider/model (the whole-resolver drop stays BY DESIGN
  per the gh-760 review). Plain `ConfigException` still maps to `_fail` for
  genuinely broken configs.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` — `UnusableRoleChainException`
  degrade base; empty-pin slot-family fallback; docs.
- `lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` (the cross-version
  slot family).
- `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart` — `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (+ the
  `KeySlotMigrationSource` record).
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `roleKeyNames` preloads the slot family.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot wiring: migration pass after preload; the roles
  block degrades on `UnusableRoleChainException`.
- `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — the incident REG test (key
  under the previous release's slot resolves); the missing-key aggregate
  re-pinned to the DEGRADE subtype (typed classification guards kept).
- `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` — 4 migration tests (copy+notice,
  canonical-populated no-op, unavailable store quiet, failing-write fallback).
- `test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` shape pins.
- `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart` — the boot-level IT
  (real binary): all-key-missing roles ⇒ exit 0, skipped entries NAMED, turn
  completes on the fallback.

## Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN, each verified against the unfixed code:
  - the incident REG test fails without the empty-pin fallback;
  - the missing-key degrade test fails while `chainFor` still throws plain
    `ConfigException`;
  - the boot IT fails (exit 254 — the exact incident brick) while the boot
    still caught only `UnknownProviderRoleException`.
- Targeted suites: `dart test test/model_roles/ test/cli/startup_test.dart
  test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart
  test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — **497 passed**.
- Boot IT (integration tag): the gh-760 poisoned-provider family incl. the new
  degrade case — green.
- `dart analyze` — 0 issues on all touched files; `dart format` clean on all
  touched files (the pre-existing whole-tree test drift is untouched, diff
  stays scoped).
- `crap4dart check --baseline` — gates pass (threshold untouched); the loc
  gate (`crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc`) passes.
- Full suite `dart test` — running against the frozen tree; result recorded in
  the run log (job `sh-71-hn60g1u9a3ygx50u`).

The Flutter app shares `ModelRolesResolver` (best-effort guarded, no
process-exit surface), so both fixes apply there unchanged.

{"content":"Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability (real incident 2026-10-12)

**Fixed on both demanded axes** — key-slot names are now treated as a cross-version contract, with resolution-level recovery AND a boot-time migration (keychain explicitly in scope):

1. **The slot family is a first-class concept**: `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})` (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) derives every slot name the SAME endpoint ever produced — the record-scoped canonical (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) plus the host-scoped shape (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the exact 1.0.556 → 1.0.564 lockout pair). The derivation itself is deliberately untouched — re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class you flagged.

2. **A key stored under the previous release's slot name still resolves** (your REG demand): the roles resolver's explicit-pin leg (`ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName`, `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) now falls back from an empty pin to the endpoint's own slot family before declaring the key missing. The incident is pinned 1:1 in `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — *"a key stored under the PREVIOUS release slot name still resolves after the record-scoped derivation moves (gh-1570 incident REG)"*: the ref pins `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`, only `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` holds the key → the chain resolves, ring base name `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`. RED against the old code (pin-empty ⇒ key-missing), GREEN after. The secrets snapshot preloads the whole family (`roleKeyNames`, `lib/src/cli/startup.dart`), so the store-backed values are actually visible to the fallback.

3. **Boot-time migration of old slots** (your Q1-mechanism demand): `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (`lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`) runs in the executable boot (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`, right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution). For every known (endpoint, record) pair — the saved custom registry's entries plus the roles chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is COPIED onto the canonical slot: non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, so a rollback keeps working), the OS keychain is explicitly in scope (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through), and each move prints a stderr notice naming both slots (never stdout — the headless events-channel rule). An unavailable or failing keychain degrades to a notice (resolution still falls back to the legacy slot) — never a boot failure. Four tests in `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` pin copy+notice, canonical-already-populated no-op, unavailable-store quiet, and failing-write fallback.

So the incident machine heals twice over: the first boot after the update migrates the stranded value onto the canonical slot (notice printed), and even without the write the resolver finds the key under the old name.

**Thread 1 (key-slot stability) — recovery + migration, derivation untouched**
(re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class being
fixed):

- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})`
  (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) — the cross-version slot family of ONE
  endpoint, canonical first: the record-scoped slot plus the host-scoped shape
  the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the incident's pair).
- `ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`)
  — an explicit pin stays first choice; an EMPTY pin now falls back to the
  endpoint's slot family before the ref is declared key-missing (the gh-1000
  AC2 hint semantics unchanged: a still-missing pin names the pin).
- `roleKeyNames` (`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`) — the secrets snapshot preloads
  the whole family (pin fallback set included), so store-backed values are
  visible to the fallback.

  `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`, wired in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`
  right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution): for every
  known (endpoint, record) pair — saved custom registry entries plus the roles
  chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is
  COPIED onto the canonical slot. Non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, a
  rollback keeps working); the OS keychain is explicitly in scope

**Fixed on both demanded axes** — key-slot names are now treated as a cross-version contract, with resolution-level recovery AND a boot-time migration (keychain explicitly in scope):

1. **The slot family is a first-class concept**: `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})` (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) derives every slot name the SAME endpoint ever produced — the record-scoped canonical (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) plus the host-scoped shape (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the exact 1.0.556 → 1.0.564 lockout pair). The derivation itself is deliberately untouched — re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class you flagged.

2. **A key stored under the previous release's slot name still resolves** (your REG demand): the roles resolver's explicit-pin leg (`ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName`, `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) now falls back from an empty pin to the endpoint's own slot family before declaring the key missing. The incident is pinned 1:1 in `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — *"a key stored under the PREVIOUS release slot name still resolves after the record-scoped derivation moves (gh-1570 incident REG)"*: the ref pins `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`, only `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` holds the key → the chain resolves, ring base name `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`. 3. **Boot-time migration of old slots** (your Q1-mechanism demand): `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (`lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`) runs in the executable boot (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`, right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution). For every known (endpoint, record) pair — the saved custom registry's entries plus the roles chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is COPIED onto the canonical slot: non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, so a rollback keeps working), the OS keychain is explicitly in scope (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through), and each move prints a stderr notice naming both slots (never stdout — the headless events-channel rule). An unavailable or failing keychain degrades to a notice (resolution still falls back to the legacy slot) — never a boot failure. {"content":"# gh-1570 rework — the two incident-driven blocking threads fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two open review threads remained after the APPROVE re-review of `24dad1d4` — both
filed from the **real incident of 2026-10-12** (a machine updating fa
`1.0.556 → 1.0.564` was bricked at boot). Both are BLOCKING and both are fixed
here with RED→GREEN tests:

1. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability.** The
   record-scoped slot derivation (`FA_KEY_<HOST>_<RECORD>`) changed meaning
   across versions and nothing recovered slots stored by older builds: the key
   existed in the secure store under the pre-update slot name
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) while the pinned slot
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) resolved empty — "missing API key". A slot
   name is a cross-version contract; a derivation change must recover old slots.
2. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCPc` — a missing key must never hard-exit the
   binary.** The aggregate outcome of an all-key-missing role chain
   (`entries.isEmpty` → plain `ConfigException` → `_fail`) process-exited the
   CLI on a RECOVERABLE condition — the user was locked out of the very tool
   the error message told them to repair with (`/key set`). gh-760 already
   established "degrade, never brick" for version skew; a missing key gets the
   same treatment.

All other threads on this PR are either resolved (fixed + replied in the
previous legs, re-reviewed APPROVE on `24dad1d4`) or machine notices; each open
thread received a reply — see `outputs/review_replies.json`.

## Approach

**Thread 1 (key-slot stability) — recovery + migration, derivation untouched**
(re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class being
fixed):

- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})`
  (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) — the cross-version slot family of ONE
  endpoint, canonical first: the record-scoped slot plus the host-scoped shape
  the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the incident's pair).
- `ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`)
  — an explicit pin stays first choice; an EMPTY pin now falls back to the
  endpoint's slot family before the ref is declared key-missing (the gh-1000
  AC2 hint semantics unchanged: a still-missing pin names the pin).
- `roleKeyNames` (`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`) — the secrets snapshot preloads
  the whole family (pin fallback set included), so store-backed values are
  visible to the fallback.
- **Boot-time migration** (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`,
  `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`, wired in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`
  right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution): for every
  known (endpoint, record) pair — saved custom registry entries plus the roles
  chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is
  COPIED onto the canonical slot. Non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, a
  rollback keeps working); the OS keychain is explicitly in scope
  (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through); each move prints a stderr notice
  naming both slots; an unavailable/failing keychain degrades to a notice
  (resolution still falls back), never a boot failure.

**Thread 2 (missing key never bricks) — typed degradable contract:**

- New `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException`
  (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) — the degradable
  "no usable chain entry" shape; `UnknownProviderRoleException` re-parented
  under it (public API compatible; version skew stays distinguishable, the
  boot treats both identically). `chainFor`'s aggregate outcome throws the
  degradable base for the key-missing shape too — the old plain
  `ConfigException` stance is what bricked the incident machine.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` catches `on UnusableRoleChainException` → loud stderr
  warning with the resolver's named skip reasons → falls back to the
  configured single provider/model (the whole-resolver drop stays BY DESIGN
  per the gh-760 review). Plain `ConfigException` still maps to `_fail` for
  genuinely broken configs.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` — `UnusableRoleChainException`
  degrade base; empty-pin slot-family fallback; docs.
- `lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` (the cross-version
  slot family).
- `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart` — `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (+ the
  `KeySlotMigrationSource` record).
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `roleKeyNames` preloads the slot family.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot wiring: migration pass after preload; the roles
  block degrades on `UnusableRoleChainException`.
- `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — the incident REG test (key
  under the previous release's slot resolves); the missing-key aggregate
  re-pinned to the DEGRADE subtype (typed classification guards kept).
- `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` — 4 migration tests (copy+notice,
  canonical-populated no-op, unavailable store quiet, failing-write fallback).
- `test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` shape pins.
- `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart` — the boot-level IT
  (real binary): all-key-missing roles ⇒ exit 0, skipped entries NAMED, turn
  completes on the fallback.

## Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN, each verified against the unfixed code:
  - the incident REG test fails without the empty-pin fallback;
  - the missing-key degrade test fails while `chainFor` still throws plain
    `ConfigException`;
  - the boot IT fails (exit 254 — the exact incident brick) while the boot
    still caught only `UnknownProviderRoleException`.
- Targeted suites: `dart test test/model_roles/ test/cli/startup_test.dart
  test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart
  test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — **497 passed**.
- Boot IT (integration tag): the gh-760 poisoned-provider family incl. the new
  degrade case — green.
- `dart analyze` — 0 issues on all touched files; `dart format` clean on all
  touched files (the pre-existing whole-tree test drift is untouched, diff
  stays scoped).
- `crap4dart check --baseline` — gates pass (threshold untouched); the loc
  gate (`crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc`) passes.
- Full suite `dart test` — running against the frozen tree; result recorded in
  the run log (job `sh-71-hn60g1u9a3ygx50u`).

The Flutter app shares `ModelRolesResolver` (best-effort guarded, no
process-exit surface), so both fixes apply there unchanged.

**Fixed on both demanded axes** — key-slot names are now treated as a cross-version contract, with resolution-level recovery AND a boot-time migration (keychain explicitly in scope):

1. **The slot family is a first-class concept**: `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})` (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) derives every slot name the SAME endpoint ever produced — the record-scoped canonical (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) plus the host-scoped shape (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the exact 1.0.556 → 1.0.564 lockout pair). The derivation itself is deliberately untouched — re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class you flagged.

2. **A key stored under the previous release's slot name still resolves** (your REG demand): the roles resolver's explicit-pin leg (`ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName`, `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) now falls back from an empty pin to the endpoint's own slot family before declaring the key missing. The incident is pinned 1:1 in `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — *"a key stored under the PREVIOUS release slot name still resolves after the record-scoped derivation moves (gh-1570 incident REG)"*: the ref pins `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`, only `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` holds the key → the chain resolves, ring base name `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`. RED against the old code (pin-empty ⇒ key-missing), GREEN after. The secrets snapshot preloads the whole family (`roleKeyNames`, `lib/src/cli/startup.dart`), so the store-backed values are actually visible to the fallback.

3. **Boot-time migration of old slots** (your Q1-mechanism demand): `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (`lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`) runs in the executable boot (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`, right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution). For every known (endpoint, record) pair — the saved custom registry's entries plus the roles chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is COPIED onto the canonical slot: non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, so a rollback keeps working), the OS keychain is explicitly in scope (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through), and each move prints a stderr notice naming both slots (never stdout — the headless events-channel rule). An unavailable or failing keychain degrades to a notice (resolution still falls back to the legacy slot) — never a boot failure. Four tests in `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` pin copy+notice, canonical-already-populated no-op, unavailable-store quiet, and failing-write fallback.

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — the two incident-driven blocking threads fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two open review threads remained after the APPROVE re-review of `24dad1d4` — both
filed from the **real incident of 2026-10-12** (a machine updating fa
`1.0.556 → 1.0.564` was bricked at boot). Both are BLOCKING and both are fixed
here with RED→GREEN tests:

1. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability.** The
   record-scoped slot derivation (`FA_KEY_<HOST>_<RECORD>`) changed meaning
   across versions and nothing recovered slots stored by older builds: the key
   existed in the secure store under the pre-update slot name
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) while the pinned slot
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) resolved empty — "missing API key". A slot
   name is a cross-version contract; a derivation change must recover old slots.
2. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCPc` — a missing key must never hard-exit the
   binary.** The aggregate outcome of an all-key-missing role chain
   (`entries.isEmpty` → plain `ConfigException` → `_fail`) process-exited the
   CLI on a RECOVERABLE condition — the user was locked out of the very tool
   the error message told them to repair with (`/key set`). gh-760 already
   established "degrade, never brick" for version skew; a missing key gets the
   same treatment.

All other threads on this PR are either resolved (fixed + replied in the
previous legs, re-reviewed APPROVE on `24dad1d4`) or machine notices; each open

## Approach

**Thread 1 (key-slot stability) — recovery + migration, derivation untouched**
(re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class being
fixed):

- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})`
  (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) — the cross-version slot family of ONE
  endpoint, canonical first: the record-scoped slot plus the host-scoped shape
  the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the incident's pair).
- `ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`)
  — an explicit pin stays first choice; an EMPTY pin now falls back to the
  endpoint's slot family before the ref is declared key-missing (the gh-1000
  AC2 hint semantics unchanged: a still-missing pin names the pin).
- `roleKeyNames` (`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`) — the secrets snapshot preloads
  the whole family (pin fallback set included), so store-backed values are
  visible to the fallback.
- **Boot-time migration** (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`,
  `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`, wired in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`
  right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution): for every
  known (endpoint, record) pair — saved custom registry entries plus the roles
  chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is
  COPIED onto the canonical slot. Non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, a
  rollback keeps working); the OS keychain is explicitly in scope
  (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through); each move prints a stderr notice
  naming both slots; an unavailable/failing keychain degrades to a notice
  (resolution still falls back), never a boot failure.

- New `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException`
  (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) — the degradable
  "no usable chain entry" shape; `UnknownProviderRoleException` re-parented
  under it (public API compatible; version skew stays distinguishable, the
  boot treats both identically). `chainFor`'s aggregate outcome throws the
  degradable base for the key-missing shape too — the old plain
  `ConfigException` stance is what bricked the incident machine.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` catches `on UnusableRoleChainException` → loud stderr
  warning with the resolver's named skip reasons → falls back to the
  configured single provider/model (the whole-resolver drop stays BY DESIGN
  per the gh-760 review). Plain `ConfigException` still maps to `_fail` for
  genuinely broken configs.

{"content":"Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability (real incident 2026-10-12)

**Fixed on both demanded axes** — key-slot names are now treated as a cross-version contract, with resolution-level recovery AND a boot-time migration (keychain explicitly in scope):

1. **The slot family is a first-class concept**: `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})` (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) derives every slot name the SAME endpoint ever produced — the record-scoped canonical (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) plus the host-scoped shape (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the exact 1.0.556 → 1.0.564 lockout pair). The derivation itself is deliberately untouched — re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class you flagged.

2. **A key stored under the previous release's slot name still resolves** (your REG demand): the roles resolver's explicit-pin leg (`ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName`, `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) now falls back from an empty pin to the endpoint's own slot family before declaring the key missing. The incident is pinned 1:1 in `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — *"a key stored under the PREVIOUS release slot name still resolves after the record-scoped derivation moves (gh-1570 incident REG)"*: the ref pins `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`, only `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` holds the key → the chain resolves, ring base name `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`. RED against the old code (pin-empty ⇒ key-missing), GREEN after. The secrets snapshot preloads the whole family (`roleKeyNames`, `lib/src/cli/startup.dart`), so the store-backed values are actually visible to the fallback.

3. **Boot-time migration of old slots** (your Q1-mechanism demand): `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (`lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`) runs in the executable boot (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`, right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution). For every known (endpoint, record) pair — the saved custom registry's entries plus the roles chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is COPIED onto the canonical slot: non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, so a rollback keeps working), the OS keychain is explicitly in scope (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through), and each move prints a stderr notice naming both slots (never stdout — the headless events-channel rule). An unavailable or failing keychain degrades to a notice (resolution still falls back to the legacy slot) — never a boot failure. Four tests in `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` pin copy+notice, canonical-already-populated no-op, unavailable-store quiet, and failing-write fallback.

So the incident machine heals twice over: the first boot after the update migrates the stranded value onto the canonical slot (notice printed), and even without the write the resolver finds the key under the old name.

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — the two incident-driven blocking threads fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two open review threads remained after the APPROVE re-review of `24dad1d4` — both
filed from the **real incident of 2026-10-12** (a machine updating fa
`1.0.556 → 1.0.564` was bricked at boot). Both are BLOCKING and both are fixed
here with RED→GREEN tests:

1. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability.** The
   record-scoped slot derivation (`FA_KEY_<HOST>_<RECORD>`) changed meaning
   across versions and nothing recovered slots stored by older builds: the key
   existed in the secure store under the pre-update slot name
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) while the pinned slot
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) resolved empty — "missing API key". A slot
   name is a cross-version contract; a derivation change must recover old slots.
2. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCPc` — a missing key must never hard-exit the
   binary.** The aggregate outcome of an all-key-missing role chain
   (`entries.isEmpty` → plain `ConfigException` → `_fail`) process-exited the
   CLI on a RECOVERABLE condition — the user was locked out of the very tool
   the error message told them to repair with (`/key set`). gh-760 already
   established "degrade, never brick" for version skew; a missing key gets the
   same treatment.

All other threads on this PR are either resolved (fixed + replied in the
previous legs, re-reviewed APPROVE on `24dad1d4`) or machine notices; each open
thread received a reply — see `outputs/review_replies.json`.

## Approach

**Thread 1 (key-slot stability) — recovery + migration, derivation untouched**
(re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class being
fixed):

- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})`
  (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) — the cross-version slot family of ONE
  endpoint, canonical first: the record-scoped slot plus the host-scoped shape
  the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the incident's pair).
- `ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`)
  — an explicit pin stays first choice; an EMPTY pin now falls back to the
  endpoint's slot family before the ref is declared key-missing (the gh-1000
  AC2 hint semantics unchanged: a still-missing pin names the pin).
- `roleKeyNames` (`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`) — the secrets snapshot preloads
  the whole family (pin fallback set included), so store-backed values are
  visible to the fallback.
- **Boot-time migration** (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`,
  `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`, wired in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`
  right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution): for every
  known (endpoint, record) pair — saved custom registry entries plus the roles
  chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is
  COPIED onto the canonical slot. Non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, a
  rollback keeps working); the OS keychain is explicitly in scope
  (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through); each move prints a stderr notice
  naming both slots; an unavailable/failing keychain degrades to a notice
  (resolution still falls back), never a boot failure.

**Thread 2 (missing key never bricks) — typed degradable contract:**

- New `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException`
  (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) — the degradable
  "no usable chain entry" shape; `UnknownProviderRoleException` re-parented
  under it (public API compatible; version skew stays distinguishable, the
  boot treats both identically). `chainFor`'s aggregate outcome throws the
  degradable base for the key-missing shape too — the old plain
  `ConfigException` stance is what bricked the incident machine.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` catches `on UnusableRoleChainException` → loud stderr
  warning with the resolver's named skip reasons → falls back to the
  configured single provider/model (the whole-resolver drop stays BY DESIGN
  per the gh-760 review). Plain `ConfigException` still maps to `_fail` for
  genuinely broken configs.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` — `UnusableRoleChainException`
  degrade base; empty-pin slot-family fallback; docs.
- `lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` (the cross-version
  slot family).
- `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart` — `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (+ the
  `KeySlotMigrationSource` record).
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `roleKeyNames` preloads the slot family.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot wiring: migration pass after preload; the roles
  block degrades on `UnusableRoleChainException`.
- `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — the incident REG test (key
  under the previous release's slot resolves); the missing-key aggregate
  re-pinned to the DEGRADE subtype (typed classification guards kept).
- `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` — 4 migration tests (copy+notice,
  canonical-populated no-op, unavailable store quiet, failing-write fallback).
- `test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` shape pins.
- `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart` — the boot-level IT
  (real binary): all-key-missing roles ⇒ exit 0, skipped entries NAMED, turn
  completes on the fallback.

## Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN, each verified against the unfixed code:
  - the incident REG test fails without the empty-pin fallback;
  - the missing-key degrade test fails while `chainFor` still throws plain
    `ConfigException`;
  - the boot IT fails (exit 254 — the exact incident brick) while the boot
    still caught only `UnknownProviderRoleException`.
- Targeted suites: `dart test test/model_roles/ test/cli/startup_test.dart
  test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart
  test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — **497 passed**.
- Boot IT (integration tag): the gh-760 poisoned-provider family incl. the new
  degrade case — green.
- `dart analyze` — 0 issues on all touched files; `dart format` clean on all
  touched files (the pre-existing whole-tree test drift is untouched, diff
  stays scoped).
- `crap4dart check --baseline` — gates pass (threshold untouched); the loc
  gate (`crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc`) passes.
- Full suite `dart test` — running against the frozen tree; result recorded in
  the run log (job `sh-71-hn60g1u9a3ygx50u`).

The Flutter app shares `ModelRolesResolver` (best-effort guarded, no
process-exit surface), so both fixes apply there unchanged.

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — the two incident-driven blocking threads fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two open review threads remained after the APPROVE re-review of `24dad1d4` — both
filed from the **real incident of 2026-10-12** (a machine updating fa
`1.0.556 → 1.0.564` was bricked at boot). Both are BLOCKING and both are fixed
here with RED→GREEN tests:

1. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability.** The
   record-scoped slot derivation (`FA_KEY_<HOST>_<RECORD>`) changed meaning
   across versions and nothing recovered slots stored by older builds: the key
   existed in the secure store under the pre-update slot name
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) while the pinned slot
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) resolved empty — "missing API key". A slot
   name is a cross-version contract; a derivation change must recover old slots.
2. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCPc` — a missing key must never hard-exit the
   binary.** The aggregate outcome of an all-key-missing role chain
   (`entries.isEmpty` → plain `ConfigException` → `_fail`) process-exited the
   CLI on a RECOVERABLE condition — the user was locked out of the very tool
   the error message told them to repair with (`/key set`). gh-760 already
   established "degrade, never brick" for version skew; a missing key gets the
   same treatment.

All other threads on this PR are either resolved (fixed + replied in the
previous legs, re-reviewed APPROVE on `24dad1d4`) or machine notices; each open
thread received a reply — see `outputs/review_replies.json`.

## Approach

**Thread 1 (key-slot stability) — recovery + migration, derivation untouched**
(re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class being
fixed):

- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})`
  (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) — the cross-version slot family of ONE
  endpoint, canonical first: the record-scoped slot plus the host-scoped shape
  the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the incident's pair).
- `ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`)
  — an explicit pin stays first choice; an EMPTY pin now falls back to the
  endpoint's slot family before the ref is declared key-missing (the gh-1000
  AC2 hint semantics unchanged: a still-missing pin names the pin).
- `roleKeyNames` (`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`) — the secrets snapshot preloads
  the whole family (pin fallback set included), so store-backed values are
  visible to the fallback.
- **Boot-time migration** (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`,
  `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`, wired in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`
  right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution): for every
  known (endpoint, record) pair — saved custom registry entries plus the roles
  chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is
  COPIED onto the canonical slot. Non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, a
  rollback keeps working); the OS keychain is explicitly in scope
  (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through); each move prints a stderr notice
  naming both slots; an unavailable/failing keychain degrades to a notice
  (resolution still falls back), never a boot failure.

**Thread 2 (missing key never bricks) — typed degradable contract:**

- New `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException`
  (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) — the degradable
  "no usable chain entry" shape; `UnknownProviderRoleException` re-parented
  under it (public API compatible; version skew stays distinguishable, the
  boot treats both identically). `chainFor`'s aggregate outcome throws the
  degradable base for the key-missing shape too — the old plain
  `ConfigException` stance is what bricked the incident machine.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` catches `on UnusableRoleChainException` → loud stderr
  warning with the resolver's named skip reasons → falls back to the
  configured single provider/model (the whole-resolver drop stays BY DESIGN
  per the gh-760 review). Plain `ConfigException` still maps to `_fail` for
  genuinely broken configs.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` — `UnusableRoleChainException`
  degrade base; empty-pin slot-family fallback; docs.
- `lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` (the cross-version
  slot family).
- `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart` — `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (+ the
  `KeySlotMigrationSource` record).
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `roleKeyNames` preloads the slot family.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot wiring: migration pass after preload; the roles
  block degrades on `UnusableRoleChainException`.
- `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — the incident REG test (key
  under the previous release's slot resolves); the missing-key aggregate
  re-pinned to the DEGRADE subtype (typed classification guards kept).
- `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` — 4 migration tests (copy+notice,
  canonical-populated no-op, unavailable store quiet, failing-write fallback).
- `test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` shape pins.
- `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart` — the boot-level IT
  (real binary): all-key-missing roles ⇒ exit 0, skipped entries NAMED, turn
  completes on the fallback.

## Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN, each verified against the unfixed code:
  - the incident REG test fails without the empty-pin fallback;
  - the missing-key degrade test fails while `chainFor` still throws plain
    `ConfigException`;
  - the boot IT fails (exit 254 — the exact incident brick) while the boot
    still caught only `UnknownProviderRoleException`.
- Targeted suites: `dart test test/model_roles/ test/cli/startup_test.dart
  test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart
  test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — **497 passed**.
- Boot IT (integration tag): the gh-760 poisoned-provider family incl. the new
  degrade case — green.
- `dart analyze` — 0 issues on all touched files; `dart format` clean on all
  touched files (the pre-existing whole-tree test drift is untouched, diff
  stays scoped).
- `crap4dart check --baseline` — gates pass (threshold untouched); the loc
  gate (`crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc`) passes.
- Full suite `dart test` — running against the frozen tree; result recorded in
  the run log (job `sh-71-hn60g1u9a3ygx50u`).

The Flutter app shares `ModelRolesResolver` (best-effort guarded, no
process-exit surface), so both fixes apply there unchanged.

{"content":"Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability (real incident 2026-10-12)

**Fixed on both demanded axes** — key-slot names are now treated as a cross-version contract, with resolution-level recovery AND a boot-time migration (keychain explicitly in scope):

1. **The slot family is a first-class concept**: `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})` (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) derives every slot name the SAME endpoint ever produced — the record-scoped canonical (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) plus the host-scoped shape (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the exact 1.0.556 → 1.0.564 lockout pair). The derivation itself is deliberately untouched — re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class you flagged.

2. **A key stored under the previous release's slot name still resolves** (your REG demand): the roles resolver's explicit-pin leg (`ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName`, `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) now falls back from an empty pin to the endpoint's own slot family before declaring the key missing. The incident is pinned 1:1 in `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — *"a key stored under the PREVIOUS release slot name still resolves after the record-scoped derivation moves (gh-1570 incident REG)"*: the ref pins `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`, only `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` holds the key → the chain resolves, ring base name `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`. RED against the old code (pin-empty ⇒ key-missing), GREEN after. The secrets snapshot preloads the whole family (`roleKeyNames`, `lib/src/cli/startup.dart`), so the store-backed values are actually visible to the fallback.

3. **Boot-time migration of old slots** (your Q1-mechanism demand): `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (`lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`) runs in the executable boot (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`, right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution). For every known (endpoint, record) pair — the saved custom registry's entries plus the roles chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is COPIED onto the canonical slot: non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, so a rollback keeps working), the OS keychain is explicitly in scope (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through), and each move prints a stderr notice naming both slots (never stdout — the headless events-channel rule). An unavailable or failing keychain degrades to a notice (resolution still falls back to the legacy slot) — never a boot failure. Four tests in `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` pin copy+notice, canonical-already-populated no-op, unavailable-store quiet, and failing-write fallback.

So the incident machine heals twice over: the first boot after the update migrates the stranded value onto the canonical slot (notice printed), and even without the write the resolver finds the key under the old name.

{"content":"# gh-1570 rework — the two incident-driven blocking threads fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two open review threads remained after the APPROVE re-review of `24dad1d4` — both
filed from the **real incident of 2026-10-12** (a machine updating fa
`1.0.556 → 1.0.564` was bricked at boot). Both are BLOCKING and both are fixed
here with RED→GREEN tests:

1. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCNr` — cross-version key-slot stability.** The
   record-scoped slot derivation (`FA_KEY_<HOST>_<RECORD>`) changed meaning
   across versions and nothing recovered slots stored by older builds: the key
   existed in the secure store under the pre-update slot name
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`) while the pinned slot
   (`FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`) resolved empty — "missing API key". A slot
   name is a cross-version contract; a derivation change must recover old slots.
2. 🚨 **`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rvCPc` — a missing key must never hard-exit the
   binary.** The aggregate outcome of an all-key-missing role chain
   (`entries.isEmpty` → plain `ConfigException` → `_fail`) process-exited the
   CLI on a RECOVERABLE condition — the user was locked out of the very tool
   the error message told them to repair with (`/key set`). gh-760 already
   established "degrade, never brick" for version skew; a missing key gets the
   same treatment.

All other threads on this PR are either resolved (fixed + replied in the
previous legs, re-reviewed APPROVE on `24dad1d4`) or machine notices; each open
thread received a reply — see `outputs/review_replies.json`.

## Approach

**Thread 1 (key-slot stability) — recovery + migration, derivation untouched**
(re-deriving would strand THIS version's slots, the very failure class being
fixed):

- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, {providerName})`
  (`lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart`) — the cross-version slot family of ONE
  endpoint, canonical first: the record-scoped slot plus the host-scoped shape
  the same endpoint wrote before the record rule (the incident's pair).
- `ModelRolesResolver._keyBaseName` (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`)
  — an explicit pin stays first choice; an EMPTY pin now falls back to the
  endpoint's slot family before the ref is declared key-missing (the gh-1000
  AC2 hint semantics unchanged: a still-missing pin names the pin).
- `roleKeyNames` (`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`) — the secrets snapshot preloads
  the whole family (pin fallback set included), so store-backed values are
  visible to the fallback.
- **Boot-time migration** (`migrateLegacyKeySlots`,
  `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart`, wired in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`
  right after the secure-store preload, BEFORE any key resolution): for every
  known (endpoint, record) pair — saved custom registry entries plus the roles
  chains' endpoints — an empty canonical slot with a populated legacy slot is
  COPIED onto the canonical slot. Non-destructive (the legacy slot stays, a
  rollback keeps working); the OS keychain is explicitly in scope
  (`SecureKeyCache.save` writes through); each move prints a stderr notice
  naming both slots; an unavailable/failing keychain degrades to a notice
  (resolution still falls back), never a boot failure.

**Thread 2 (missing key never bricks) — typed degradable contract:**

- New `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException`
  (`lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart`) — the degradable
  "no usable chain entry" shape; `UnknownProviderRoleException` re-parented
  under it (public API compatible; version skew stays distinguishable, the
  boot treats both identically). `chainFor`'s aggregate outcome throws the
  degradable base for the key-missing shape too — the old plain
  `ConfigException` stance is what bricked the incident machine.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` catches `on UnusableRoleChainException` → loud stderr
  warning with the resolver's named skip reasons → falls back to the
  configured single provider/model (the whole-resolver drop stays BY DESIGN
  per the gh-760 review). Plain `ConfigException` still maps to `_fail` for
  genuinely broken configs.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/model_roles/model_resolver.dart` — `UnusableRoleChainException`
  degrade base; empty-pin slot-family fallback; docs.
- `lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` (the cross-version
  slot family).
- `lib/src/cli/headless_provider_key.dart` — `migrateLegacyKeySlots` (+ the
  `KeySlotMigrationSource` record).
- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — `roleKeyNames` preloads the slot family.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot wiring: migration pass after preload; the roles
  block degrades on `UnusableRoleChainException`.
- `test/model_roles/model_resolver_test.dart` — the incident REG test (key
  under the previous release's slot resolves); the missing-key aggregate
  re-pinned to the DEGRADE subtype (typed classification guards kept).
- `test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart` — 4 migration tests (copy+notice,
  canonical-populated no-op, unavailable store quiet, failing-write fallback).
- `test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — `keySlotCandidates` shape pins.
- `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart` — the boot-level IT
  (real binary): all-key-missing roles ⇒ exit 0, skipped entries NAMED, turn
  completes on the fallback.

## Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN, each verified against the unfixed code:
  - the incident REG test fails without the empty-pin fallback;
  - the missing-key degrade test fails while `chainFor` still throws plain
    `ConfigException`;
  - the boot IT fails (exit 254 — the exact incident brick) while the boot
    still caught only `UnknownProviderRoleException`.
- Targeted suites: `dart test test/model_roles/ test/cli/startup_test.dart
  test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/cli/headless_provider_key_test.dart
  test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` — **497 passed**.
- Boot IT (integration tag): the gh-760 poisoned-provider family incl. the new
  degrade case — green.
- `dart analyze` — 0 issues on all touched files; `dart format` clean on all
  touched files (the pre-existing whole-tree test drift is untouched, diff
  stays scoped).
- `crap4dart check --baseline` — gates pass (threshold untouched); the loc
  gate (`crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc`) passes.
- Full suite `dart test` — running against the frozen tree; result recorded in
  the run log (job `sh-71-hn60g1u9a3ygx50u`).

The Flutter app shares `ModelRolesResolver` (best-effort guarded, no
process-exit surface), so both fixes apply there unchanged.
